claims.head: Carolina should get plenty of shots away
claims.body: Few teams shoot as often as Carolina: 65.8 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5, 3rd in the league. Chicago sits 26th of 32 at keeping shots down.

claims.head: Chicago pounces on mistakes, and Carolina makes them
claims.body: Carolina gives up more dangerous chances after losing the puck than most (24th of 32 at avoiding breakdowns). Chicago ranks 9th for chances off turnovers.

notes.text: S. Jarvis has not played this season. W. Carrier is in his usual spot beside S. Aho and A. Svechnikov, up from fourth-line minutes last season. That line is getting 9:15 a game at 5-on-5, down from 10:44 with Jarvis. J. Kotkaniemi has moved into Carrier’s old spot beside M. Jankowski and E. Robinson.
L. Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: J. Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 68% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 61 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by N. Ehlers (15 of 18 changes).

notes.text: T. Teravainen is no longer playing on the power play: 0% of the team’s power-play time in 3 games, down from 58% last season.

CHI.head: Chicago has its work cut out
CHI.body: Carolina has controlled the play far better over recent games and Chicago has home ice. Chicago could still pull it off if it pounces on loose pucks, but it might need a miracle.

CAR.head: Carolina has nearly everything going for it
CAR.body: Carolina has controlled the play far better over recent games and Chicago has home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Chicago can make a game of it if it pounces on loose pucks.
